questions.q: Why do AI labs typically publish GPU-hours rather than a dollar figure for a training run?
options: Dollar figures are classified information in every jurisdiction
GPU-hours are a hardware-neutral measure, while real negotiated $/GPU-hour pricing varies widely by provider and commitment
GPU-hours are always lower than the equivalent dollar amount
Dollar amounts cannot be calculated for any cloud GPU
questions.explain: GPU-hours describe actual compute consumed regardless of what was paid for it, while real-world $/GPU-hour pricing depends heavily on provider, negotiated rates, and timing -- making GPU-hours the more stable, comparable figure to publish.

questions.q: Which of the following is a real cost category NOT captured by a simple FLOPs-based compute formula?
options: The number of attention heads in the model
Failed and restarted training runs that re-spend GPU-hours on the same stretch of training
The vocabulary size of the tokenizer
The model's parameter count
questions.explain: A FLOPs formula estimates ideal compute for a successful run, but real training involves hardware failures and instability that force restarts, effectively spending GPU-hours twice on recovered segments.

questions.q: What distinction does 'cost of a run' vs. 'cost of a capability' describe?
options: There is no meaningful distinction; they are always equal
A published GPU-hour figure usually covers only the final successful run, not the larger research investment (ablations, experiments) that informed it
Cost of a capability only applies to alignment, never pretraining
Cost of a run refers only to inference costs after deployment
questions.explain: The GPU-hours disclosed in a technical report typically describe just the final large-scale run. Reaching that point usually required a much larger total investment in smaller ablations and experiments.

questions.q: Why does evaluation contribute meaningfully to overall training-run cost, beyond a single final benchmark run?
options: Evaluation is run once, after the model is fully trained and deployed
Evaluation is typically repeated across many checkpoints throughout training, not performed only at the end
Evaluation requires no compute at all
Evaluation replaces the need for a data pipeline
questions.explain: Candidate checkpoints are evaluated against benchmarks and held-out data repeatedly throughout a run to track progress, which adds up across the full training timeline rather than being a single end-of-run cost.

questions.q: Besides compute, data, and evaluation, which other cost category does a complete training-run cost estimate need to include?
options: Engineering and research headcount, plus storage and networking infrastructure
The number of app downloads for the resulting product
The color scheme of the model's documentation website
The number of social media mentions the model receives
questions.explain: The people designing the architecture and tuning the pipeline, plus storage for large checkpoints and high-bandwidth interconnect for distributed training, are real costs that don't appear in a FLOPs formula.
